goal: Move ownership of the txindex, txospenderindex, coinstatsindex and block filter indexes from process-global unique_ptrs into NodeContext.
Removes remaining global index state so indexes can be maintained and tested independently and so the node can eventually run as a separate process.
reviewability: Ready to review now, code is rebased and CI is clean.
Author has kept it current through two rebases, most recently 2026-09-15.
agreement: Two concept ACKs with no stated objections (sedited, fjahr).
No reviewer has raised a harm or blocking concern; discussion only clarified overlap with #24230 (Sjors, w0xlt).

result.summary: This PR removes the last process-global index singletons (g_txindex, g_txospenderindex, g_coin_stats_index, g_filter_indexes) and moves ownership of these index objects into NodeContext. A non-owning node.indexes list remains for shared startup/shutdown and getindexinfo, and PeerManager now receives a lookup callback instead of reaching into a global filter-index map. The author states behavior is unchanged: same startup options, same init step, and indexes are still destroyed while validation_signals is alive so they can unregister safely.
result.problem: Global index singletons make indexes hard to reason about, test in isolation, or run outside the main process, which is a friction point for anyone working on indexes or on the multiprocess/IPC direction. The PR removes this remaining global state so index lifetime is scoped to NodeContext instead of process-wide statics.

resolved_concerns: Sjors asked how this interacts with #24230; w0xlt explained the two PRs are conceptually orthogonal (24230 changes sync logic, this PR changes ownership) though they will conflict mechanically on rebase.

categories.name: indexes
categories.evidence: Primary subject: moves txindex, txospenderindex, coinstatsindex, and blockfilterindex ownership out of process-global statics into NodeContext, and introduces node/indexes.{h,cpp} to house the block filter index registry. Matches the 'UTXO Db and Indexes' label directly.
categories.rationale: The indexes category values 'decoupling indexes from node internals so they can be maintained and tested independently' as a mid-tier concern, and this PR is squarely that: it removes the last global index singletons and scopes their lifetime to NodeContext, which the author argues is 'aligned with the multiprocess direction anyway.' No correctness bug or performance change is claimed or evidenced; behavior is explicitly stated to be unchanged. It is a durable maintainability improvement with a plausible link to future multiprocess work, but not urgent or fund/consensus critical, so P2 rather than P1.

uncertainties: Whether this PR is a hard prerequisite for any specific multiprocess/IPC PR was not stated explicitly beyond the author's general remark that it is 'aligned with the multiprocess direction'; the conflicts list is speculative evidence, not a stated dependency.

The many call-site changes in rpc/rest/wallet-test/net_processing files are treated as mechanical follow-on from the ownership move rather than substantive changes to those areas; a reviewer in those areas might disagree given the file count touched.
result.card: This PR moves ownership of the txindex, txospenderindex, coinstatsindex, and block filter indexes from process-global unique_ptrs into NodeContext, replacing global lookup functions with NodeContext-scoped equivalents and a small PeerManager callback for filter-index lookup. It solves an internal design problem: global index state is a longstanding wart the author says is 'aligned with the multiprocess direction,' since indexes cannot easily be maintained or tested independently while global. Behavior is explicitly unchanged; this is a structural/maintainability change rather than a bug fix or feature. Two maintainers gave concept ACKs (sedited, fjahr) with no objections, and the only question raised (interaction with #24230) was answered without dispute. The PR is clean, CI-passing, and has been kept rebased twice by the author, most recently 2026-09-15, so it is ready for code review now.
